summary: Norway is a unitary state. The Storting sets all taxes and the Tax Administration collects them, but the 22% tax on general income is shared: most of it goes to the municipalities and counties. The State’s own big flows are the VAT, the National Insurance contributions, the income taxes of companies and, uniquely, a petroleum income tax of 78% on net income from oil and gas production, which in the list brings in about as much as the VAT. The net wealth tax is also mostly local.
structureNote: The figures are the Commission’s National Tax List for 2024, in NOK million; several of the largest lines are given as round numbers (VAT 390,000, local and regional income tax 350,000, petroleum taxes 100,000 and 281,000), so they are rounded values. The income tax of individuals and the net wealth tax are each drawn twice, as the State’s and the municipalities’ and counties’ part, using Eurostat’s split of the same year. The imputed tax on emission permits (NOK 2.5 billion) and the employers’ imputed social contributions (NOK 8.3 billion) are left out. The social contributions are drawn under the State.

theme.motifNote: Topographic contour lines over the outline of Norway (the generic motif; no bespoke art yet).

levels.description: The Storting legislates all taxes; the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) collects them and the National Insurance contributions, which fund the National Insurance Scheme.
levels.fiscalPower: The Storting sets the rates and bases of all taxes each year; municipalities set only the real estate tax rate within a ceiling.

levels.description: The municipalities and the county authorities. They receive most of the tax on general income and the net wealth tax, and the municipalities that choose to levy it receive the real estate tax; they also receive the natural resource tax from power plants.
levels.fiscalPower: The Storting fixes the income tax rates for the local level; municipalities decide whether to levy a real estate tax.

denominators.label: State taxes (National Tax List), 2024
denominators.definition: The taxes on production and imports, on income and wealth, and on capital that the National Tax List books to the State, other than the local lines and the imputed tax on emission permits; includes the State’s part of the income tax of individuals and of the net wealth tax.
denominators.locator: Sheet NO, 2024, the lines listed with each tax
denominators.calculation: Sum of the 19 tax rows below (NOK million)
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024; the list's cut-off was 30 October 2025. Several large lines are rounded. Vintage check against Eurostat's July 2026 accounts: D2: NTL 530,939, Eurostat July 2026 528,240; D5: NTL 1,068,771, Eurostat July 2026 1,079,047; D61: NTL 497,915, Eurostat July 2026 501,929.

denominators.label: Social contributions paid by employers, 2024
denominators.definition: The actual employers’ contributions (National Insurance, the Public Service Pension Fund and the seamen’s scheme); imputed contributions are left out.
denominators.locator: Sheet NO, 2024, lines D611 C01 to C03
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024, same list and cut-off as the taxes.

denominators.label: Social contributions paid by employees, 2024
denominators.definition: The employees’ contributions to the National Insurance, the Public Service Pension Fund and the seamen’s and fishermen’s arrangements.
denominators.locator: Sheet NO, 2024, lines D613CE C01 to C04
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024, same list and cut-off as the taxes.

denominators.label: Contributions of the self-employed and pensioners, 2024
denominators.definition: The contributions of the self-employed and of pensioners to the National Insurance.
denominators.locator: Sheet NO, 2024, lines D613CS and D613CN
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024, same list and cut-off as the taxes.

denominators.label: Income tax received by the municipalities and counties, 2024
denominators.definition: The part of the income tax of individuals that Eurostat’s accounts record under local government.
denominators.caveat: Eurostat July 2026 vintage, a different release from the National Tax List.

denominators.label: Net wealth tax recorded under local government, 2024
denominators.definition: The part of the net wealth tax that Eurostat’s accounts record under local government.
denominators.caveat: Eurostat July 2026 vintage, a different release from the National Tax List.

denominators.label: Real estate tax of the municipalities, 2024
denominators.definition: The real estate tax levied by the municipalities that choose to.
denominators.caveat: Eurostat books NOK 17,536 million of taxes on production under local government, which is this tax.

denominators.label: Natural resource tax, 2024
denominators.definition: The tax on hydropower production that goes to the municipalities and counties.
denominators.caveat: Eurostat books NOK 1,632 million of corporate income taxes under local government, which equals this line.

sizing.label: Taxes and compulsory social contributions of all levels of government
sizing.definition: The taxes of the State and of the municipalities and counties plus the actual social contributions, calendar 2024, as listed in the National Tax List and split by Eurostat. Excludes the imputed tax on emission permits and imputed social contributions.
